lines.japanese: てなわけで、本日も混雑してまいりました夕食時のアレキサンダー！
lines.english: And so we return to Alexander at dinnertime, where the crowds are gathering once again!

lines.japanese: 「いらっしゃいませ！　ただいま満席ですので、こちらに名前を書いてもうしばらくお待ちいただけますか！」
lines.english: “Welcome! We're currently full, so could you write your name here and wait just a little longer?”

lines.japanese: 「灰皿ですね？　ハイただいまお持ちいたします！　コーヒーのお代わりはいかがでしょうか！」
lines.english: “An ashtray? Certainly, I'll bring one right away! Would you care for another cup of coffee?”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとうございました！　またのご来店をお待ちしております！」
lines.english: “Thank you very much! We look forward to serving you again!”

lines.japanese: 「ほう、今日の鷲介は一段と動きがいいな。さては昨日、自慰行為を自制したな？」
lines.english: “Ah, Shusuke is moving with unusual vigor today. You refrained from pleasuring yourself yesterday, didn't you?”

lines.japanese: 「それではお客様、ご案内いたします！」
lines.english: “Allow me to show you to your table!”

lines.japanese: 「よし、今日はよく働いている褒美として、ピンフ通りの裏ＤＶＤ屋へ連れていってやる。ククク、俺たちの新しいドリームを１２枚１万円で手に入れようぜ。ただし明日の仕事に支障がない程度にしておけよ」
lines.english: “Very well. As a reward for your excellent work today, I'll take you to the bootleg-DVD shop behind Pinfu Street. Heh heh. Let us purchase twelve new dreams for ten thousand yen. But take care not to impair your performance tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: 「恐れいります、ありがとうございました！」
lines.english: “Thank you very much. We appreciate your patronage!”

lines.japanese: 「はっはっは、そんな丁寧にお辞儀をするほど感謝しなくてもいいぞ。俺とおまえの仲じゃないか。照れるな照れるな」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha! There is no need to bow so politely in gratitude. You and I are comrades, are we not? No need to be bashful.”

lines.japanese: 「ああもう、この忙しいときにツッコミ入れさせないでくださいよ！　働け！　働けーっ！」
lines.english: “Oh, come on! We're too busy for me to stop and answer every stupid thing you say! Work! Get to work!”

lines.japanese: 「まあ待て。忙しいときにも多少のゆとりを持たねば、足元の不注意でスッ転ぶものだぞ。張りきってもらうのはありがたいが、多少の力は抜いておけ」
lines.english: “Now, now. If you leave yourself no breathing room when things are busy, one careless step may send you sprawling. I appreciate your enthusiasm, but learn to ease up a little.”

lines.japanese: ああ、たしかに俺、さっき階段でスッ転んだな。なるほど、多少は力を抜けか。マスターって、たまーに良いこと言うんだよな。
lines.english: True. I had fallen down the stairs earlier. So I ought to ease up a little. The boss did occasionally say something worthwhile.

lines.japanese: 「ちなみに俺は毎日抜いてるぞ。なんちゃって」
lines.english: “For the record, I get off every day. Ha!”

lines.japanese: だけどこういう駄オチを付けたがるから、手放しには尊敬できないんだよなあ。分かっててやってるんでしょうけど。
lines.english: That compulsion to tack on lousy punch lines was why I could never respect him outright. Not that he didn't know exactly what he was doing.

lines.japanese: 「まあおまえもあまり気張らずに、事務室で女子のユニフォームでも着て……ん？」
lines.english: “In any event, don't strain yourself. Perhaps you could relax in the office wearing one of the women's uniforms... Hmm?”

lines.japanese: 「なんすか？　言っとくけど俺、そんな真似してませんからね」
lines.english: “What is it? For the record, I haven’t done anything like that.”

lines.japanese: 「くんくん、くんくん」
lines.english: “Sniff, sniff. Sniff, sniff.”

lines.japanese: 「む……おかしいな鷲介、おまえの服から女の匂いがするぞ」
lines.english: “Hmm... How strange, Shusuke. Your clothes smell of a woman.”
“Pfft!”

lines.japanese: 「おいなんだ、おまえもしかして自慰行為どころか生殖行為に及んだのか」
lines.english: “Good heavens. Have you progressed beyond self-pleasure to actual procreation?”

lines.japanese: 「ななななに言ってるんですか！　そそそそんなわけないじゃないですか！　こちとら青春の入り口が羅生門ってくらいのストイックな人間ですよ」
lines.english: “Wh-wh-what are you talking about? O-of course not! I'm so ascetic that the gateway to my youth might as well be Rashomon!”

lines.japanese: 「くんくん……むむ、しかもまだ新しい匂いだな。なんだなんだ仕事中に。おい貴様、俺に内緒で何をしていた。さわりの部分だけでいいから話してみろ」
lines.english: “Sniff, sniff... Hmm. And the scent is fresh. What have you been doing in the middle of work? Confess. Just tell me the climax.”

lines.japanese: 「ちなみに『さわり』という言葉は、話の冒頭という意味で使われることが多いですが、本来は義太夫節における話の聞かせ所、つまりサビやクライマックスのことを指します」
lines.english: “Incidentally, people often use ‘climax’ to mean any exciting part, but strictly speaking it is the point of greatest dramatic tension near the end.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、何もしてませんから。何も話せませんから。おおっと、お客様いらっしゃいませーえ！」
lines.english: “I haven't done anything, so there's nothing to tell you. Oh! Welcome, honored guests!”

lines.japanese: 俺は仕事に忙殺されるこの状況をありがたく思いつつ、マスターの前から逃げだしました。
lines.english: Grateful to have work to bury myself in, I fled from the boss.

lines.japanese: 「ふん、あの匂いは彼女の……まあいい、業務に支障をきたさない範囲でやれよ」
lines.english: “Hmph. That scent belongs to... Well, never mind. Do as you please, provided it doesn't interfere with your duties.”

lines.japanese: 彼は俺の方を見て、小憎らしい笑みを浮かべつつ親指を立てていました。
lines.english: He looked my way, raised his thumb, and gave me a maddeningly knowing smile.

lines.japanese: さ、さすがの嗅覚……。
lines.english: Th-that nose of his was formidable...

lines.japanese: さて、混雑も落ち着いて一段落。
lines.english: At last the crowd thinned and business settled down.

lines.japanese: そろそろ休憩の時間にならないっすかねー。なんて思いつつ日和子さんの姿を探してしまう俺。
lines.english: Wasn't it nearly time for my break? Even as I wondered, my eyes went searching for Hiyoko.

lines.japanese: いやあ、こうしてボケーッてしてると、いつもみたく後ろから日和子さんの怒鳴り声が飛んでくるんじゃないかなあって──
lines.english: Standing around in a daze like this, I almost expected Hiyoko's usual angry shout to come flying from behind me—

lines.japanese: 「だから悪かったって言ってるじゃないですか！」
lines.english: “I told you I was sorry!”

lines.japanese: ──あれ、ほんとに来た。
lines.english: —oh. There it was.

lines.japanese: や、違うな、この声は俺に向けられたものじゃない。なんだろう、穏やかじゃないな。
lines.english: No, wait. That wasn't directed at me. Whatever was happening, it didn't sound good.

lines.japanese: とりあえず声がした事務室へ向かいました。
lines.english: I headed for the office, where the voice had come from.

lines.japanese: 「すいません、お邪魔しまー……」
lines.english: “Excuse me. Pardon the interrup—”

lines.japanese: 「ぜんぜん悪いと思ってないだろ！？　おまえ、いい加減にしろよ！」
lines.english: “You don't feel sorry at all! Enough is enough!”

lines.japanese: そうっと扉を開くと、俺の声など届かないくらいの剣幕で言い争う日和子さんと英里子さんの姿がありました。
lines.english: I eased open the door and found Hiyoko and Eriko arguing so fiercely that my voice never reached them.

lines.japanese: ただいつもの光景と違うのは、日和子さんが珍しく……いや、俺が知っている中では初めて、英里子さんにガチで言いかえしています。
lines.english: What set this apart from the usual scene was that Hiyoko was actually arguing back at Eriko—something rare, or rather, something I had never seen her do before.

lines.japanese: 「だから謝ってるじゃないですか！　これ以上どうしてほしいんですか！」
lines.english: “I said I was sorry! What else do you want from me?”

lines.japanese: 「どうしろとかじゃなくてさ、私はおまえが何してたのかを聞いてんだよ」
lines.english: “It isn't about what I want. I'm asking what you were doing.”

lines.japanese: 「それはっ……その、少しの間フロアにいなかったことは謝ります……具合が悪くて休んでたんです」
lines.english: “I... I'm sorry I was away from the floor for a little while... I wasn't feeling well, so I took a rest.”

lines.japanese: フロアにいなかったって、もしかして日和子さんさっきの……それで英里子さんと言い争ってる？
lines.english: Away from the floor—did she mean what Hiyoko and I had done earlier? Was that why she was arguing with Eriko?

lines.japanese: 俺は部屋の中に入ったものの、なにも出来ず馬鹿みたいにドアの横で突ったっていました。
lines.english: I had entered the room, but I could do nothing. I merely stood beside the door like an idiot.

lines.japanese: 「おー、たまひよ。おまえ、私の目ぇ見てホントのこと言ってみ」
lines.english: “All right, Tama-chick. Look me in the eye and tell me the truth.”

lines.japanese: それまで英里子さんに立ちむかっていた日和子さんでしたが、顔の両側を掴まれて迫られると、脅えているのを耐えるようにして黙りこんでしまいました。
lines.english: Until then Hiyoko had faced Eriko squarely, but when Eriko caught her face between both hands and leaned close, she fell silent as though struggling not to show her fear.

lines.japanese: 俺も気がついていました。一見すると、何者にも怯むことなく立ちむかうように見える日和子さん。
lines.english: I had noticed it too. At first glance, Hiyoko seemed ready to confront anyone without flinching.

lines.japanese: そんな彼女の弱点は、まっすぐに目を見据えること。彼女は相手の正面に立って顔を見ることが出来ても、正面から向けられる相手の視線には目を合わせられないひとなのです。
lines.english: But her weakness was being looked straight in the eye. She could stand face-to-face with someone and look at them, yet she couldn't meet their gaze when they looked straight back.

lines.japanese: どんなに自分が正しくても、いや、正しすぎる日和子さんだからこそ、言いかえせなくなった相手に向けられる無言の非難に耐えられなかったのかもしれません。
lines.english: No matter how right she was—or perhaps precisely because Hiyoko was so painfully conscientious—she could not endure the silent accusation of someone she no longer knew how to answer.

lines.japanese: 俺はそんな優しい日和子さんが大好きです。
lines.english: I loved that gentleness in her.

lines.japanese: それと同時に、こんな状況が来ることを心配もしていました。
lines.english: At the same time, I had worried that a situation like this might come.

lines.japanese: 英里子さんは、俺よりも日和子さんとの付き合いが長いひとです。そんなことはとっくに気がついているでしょう。
lines.english: Eriko had known Hiyoko much longer than I had. Surely she had noticed this weakness long ago.

lines.japanese: 「別に少しくらいサボってたからって怒んねーよ。だけどおまえ、いま私に嘘ついたよな？」
lines.english: “I wouldn't be angry just because you slacked off for a few minutes. But you just lied to me, didn't you?”

lines.japanese: 少しでも顔が逸れそうになると、英里子さんの手は日和子さんの顔を押さえつけて正面へ戻します。
lines.english: Whenever Hiyoko's face began to turn aside, Eriko's hands forced it forward again.

lines.japanese: 「嘘なんか……」
lines.english: “I didn’t lie…”

lines.japanese: 「だから私の目を見て言えって。たまひよおまえさ、嘘つけないんだよ」
lines.english: “I said look me in the eye. Tama-chick, you can't lie.”

lines.japanese: 「すみませんでした」
lines.english: “I’m sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「なにがすみませんなんだよ。謝るなら何してたか説明したっていいんじゃないの？」
lines.english: “Sorry for what? If you're apologizing, why can't you explain what you were doing?”

lines.japanese: 「普段ひとには注意するくせに、はっ、姿消して戻ってきたと思ったら機嫌良さそうにしちゃって」
lines.english: “You spend all your time correcting everyone else, then you vanish and come back looking pleased with yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「べつに、機嫌よさそうになんてしてません……！」
lines.english: “I did not look pleased with myself...!”

lines.japanese: 「よーし、正面からまっすぐ私の目を見て話せ」
lines.english: “Good. Then look me straight in the eye and say that.”

lines.japanese: 「……すみません」
lines.english: “…I’m sorry.”

lines.japanese: 言い争いというよりも、英里子さんが日和子さんを一方的に攻撃しているような構図になってきました。
lines.english: This was less an argument now than Eriko attacking Hiyoko outright.

lines.japanese: ここで俺が間に入れば、いつも通りなあなあで済むのかもしれません。
lines.english: If I stepped between them, perhaps I could smooth things over as we usually did.

lines.japanese: だけどあの時間、懸命に働いていた英里子さんを見ている俺は、拳を握りしめただけで、やっぱりただ突ったっていることしかできませんでした。
lines.english: But I had seen Eriko working her heart out during that time. I could only clench my fists and remain where I was.

lines.japanese: 「おまえさ、自分だけが真面目にやってると思ってンのかもしンないけど、そんなんただの思いあがりだからな？」
lines.english: “Maybe you think you're the only one here who takes her job seriously, but that's nothing but arrogance.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　自分がいつでも正しいと思ってんの？　甘ったれてんじゃねーよ。そんな風に中途半端にやられたらこっちも困るんだよ」
lines.english: “What? You think you're always right? Don't be such a spoiled brat. When you half-ass things like this, you make trouble for the rest of us.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ、言いたいことあんなら言えよ。なんでそこで黙っちゃうんだよ」
lines.english: “What is it? If you've got something to say, say it. Why clam up now?”

lines.japanese: 英里子さんの口調が段々と鋭さを増してきました。
lines.english: Eriko's tone grew sharper with every word.

lines.japanese: 「そんなにひとの目が怖いなら、自分の書いたものを読んでもらおうなんて思うなよ」
lines.english: “If you're that terrified of people looking at you, don't ask them to read what you write.”

lines.japanese: 「べつに周りの目なんて気にしてません」
lines.english: “I don't care what other people think.”

lines.japanese: 「へ～え？　じゃあ、なんで二作目で作風変えたんだよ。ああそうだ、おまえの書きたいものってなんなのか、いまここで私に言ってみ」
lines.english: “Oh, really? Then why did you change your style for the second book? Better yet, tell me right now: what is it that you want to write?”

lines.japanese: 「だからっ、私の作品とは関係ないじゃないですかっ……！　いい加減にしてください！」
lines.english: “I told you, this has nothing to do with my work...! Enough!”

lines.japanese: 「関係ない関係ないっておまえ、ここまで自分の書いたもん好きに言われて、言いかえすことも出来ないのかよ。悔しくないわけ？」
lines.english: “You keep saying this has nothing to do with your writing, but I've said whatever I pleased about it right to your face and you still can't talk back. Doesn't that piss you off?”

lines.japanese: 「だって！」
lines.english: “Because!”

lines.japanese: 「私だって、少しでも色んな人に読んでもらえるよう、試行錯誤して……」
lines.english: “I've been trying everything I can to make my work reach more people...”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　おまえさっき言ったよな、周りの目なんか気にしないって。あーあ、言ってることが矛盾してんじゃん」
lines.english: “What? You just said you don't care what people think. Listen to yourself—you're contradicting yourself already.”

lines.japanese: 「で、おまえの書きたいものってなんなの」
lines.english: “So what do you want to write?”

lines.japanese: 「結局答えらんないのかよ。書きたいものが分からないから、読んでる方にもおまえが何を言いたいのか伝わンないんじゃねーの？」
lines.english: “You still can't answer. Maybe readers can't understand what you're trying to say because you don't know what you want to write in the first place.”

lines.japanese: 「もう私が悪かったって認めてるんですから……いいじゃないですかっ」
lines.english: “I've already admitted I was wrong... Isn't that enough?”

lines.japanese: 顔を伏せてしまったのでここから日和子さんの表情を知るすべはありませんが、声の合間に鼻をすする音が聞こえてきます。
lines.english: She had lowered her face, so I could no longer see her expression from where I stood. But between her words, I heard her sniff.

lines.japanese: 俺は握っていた手に強く力を込めました。
lines.english: I clenched my fists harder.

lines.japanese: 「はあ、ごめんなさいって言えばなんでも許してもらえんの。ホントおまえ、おめでたいな。そんなに周りから愛されてると思ってんの」
lines.english: “Oh, so saying sorry means everybody has to forgive you? You really do live in a happy little world. You think everyone loves you that much?”

lines.japanese: 「そんなんだから、三作目だっていつまでも世に出ねーで宙ぶらりんなんだよ」
lines.english: “That's why your third book still hasn't seen the light of day. It's been left hanging in limbo all this time.”

lines.japanese: その瞬間、日和子さんが顔を上げました。その表情は気丈で、唇を横に結んではいたけど――
lines.english: At that, Hiyoko raised her head. Her expression was resolute, her lips pressed into a firm line, but—

lines.japanese: ──目から零れたしずくが、線になって頬を伝っていきました。
lines.english: —a drop spilled from her eye and traced a line down her cheek.

lines.japanese: 日和子さんは涙を隠すように両手で顔を覆うと、そのまま英里子さんの前から逃げだしてしまいました。
lines.english: Hiyoko covered her face with both hands to hide her tears, then fled from Eriko.

lines.japanese: 「あ！　おい、待てって！」
lines.english: “Ah! Hey, wait!”

lines.japanese: 俺の目の前を通り過ぎるとき、日和子さんの口が、一瞬だけ動いたように見えました。気のせいかもしれないけど、ほんのわずか開いたような……。
lines.english: As she passed me, I thought I saw Hiyoko's mouth move for just an instant. Perhaps I imagined it, but her lips seemed to part ever so slightly...

lines.japanese: 「ああもう、何なんだっつの！」
lines.english: “Oh, for God's sake! What the hell was that?”

lines.japanese: 英里子さんは俺に背中を向けて、事務室のソファーにどっかと座りました。
lines.english: Eriko turned her back on me and dropped heavily onto the office sofa.

lines.japanese: 「で。おまえはそこで何してんの」
lines.english: “So. What are you doing standing there?”

lines.japanese: 「や、休憩でも取ろうかと思ってきたんすけど……そんな空気でもないみたいっすね」
lines.english: “I came in here to take a break... but I guess this isn't the right atmosphere.”

lines.japanese: 俺は彼女の正面に回ると、目線を合わせるためソファーに腰を下ろしました。
lines.english: I circled around to face her and sat on the sofa so our eyes were level.

lines.japanese: 「えーと、どうでもい……くないことなんですけどー」
lines.english: “Um, this may be none of my business... except it isn't, so...”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　俺の日和子さんをいじめるなーって？　言っとくけどおまえ、ダセえ恋愛すんなよ」
lines.english: “What? Going to tell me not to bully your precious Hiyoko? Listen, don't be such a loser when it comes to love.”

lines.japanese: 「彼女を泣かせたやつ＝悪なんて安直に決めつけて、ソッコー喰ってかかるようなのは『彼女を守る』なんて言わねーからな」
lines.english: “If you jump straight to ‘whoever made her cry is evil’ and go after them on the spot, don’t call that ‘protecting her.’”

lines.japanese: 「いやー、ていうか、俺まだ彼氏じゃないっす。返事待ちっす」
lines.english: “Actually, I'm not her boyfriend yet. I'm waiting for her answer.”

lines.japanese: 英里子さんは一瞬目を丸くしたものの、すぐにフンと笑って、膝の上の脚を組みかえました。
lines.english: Eriko's eyes widened for an instant. Then she snorted, crossed one leg over the other, and settled back.

lines.japanese: 「千歳、オトコの価値がどこで測られるか教えてやろうか。彼女の女友達が交わす雑談の中だよ」
lines.english: “Chitose, want me to tell you where a man's worth is measured? In the casual gossip among his girlfriend's friends.”

lines.japanese: 「痘痕も笑窪ってゆーだろ、彼女が彼氏をカッケーなんて思うのは当然。千歳、おまえは彼女の女友達にまでカッケーと思われるオトコんなれよ」
lines.english: “Love is blind. Of course a girl thinks her own boyfriend is cool. Become the kind of man even her friends think is cool.”

lines.japanese: 「えーと日野先生、質問です」
lines.english: “Professor Hino, I have a question.”

lines.japanese: 「なに」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「英里子さんと日和子さんはお友達という認識でよろしいのでしょうか」
lines.english: “Am I correct in understanding that you and Hiyoko are friends?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、私はそう思ってるよ。向こうがどうだかは知んないけど」
lines.english: “Yeah. That's what I think. No idea what she thinks.”

lines.japanese: ふう、と前髪をひと吹き。
lines.english: I blew my bangs out of my eyes.

lines.japanese: 「英里子さんって、日和子さんのことべつに嫌いじゃないんすよね？　なんであんな言い方するんすか？」
lines.english: “You don't actually dislike Hiyoko, do you? Then why talk to her like that?”

lines.japanese: 「なに、あんな言い方って」
lines.english: “Like what?”

lines.japanese: 「明らかに感情入ってるじゃないすか。英里子さんってあんまマジギレしてガー言うひとじゃないっすよね？　嫌いだったら相手にしないでガンスルーしちゃうひとじゃないすか」
lines.english: “You were obviously emotional. You don't usually get genuinely pissed and start yelling, do you? If you hated somebody, you'd ignore them completely and never bother.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで日和子さんに対してはそうなのかなーって思って」
lines.english: “So I'm wondering why you're like that with Hiyoko.”

lines.japanese: 英里子さんはいつも通りの強さを持った瞳で俺のことをまっすぐに見据えました。
lines.english: Eriko fixed me with her usual strong, unwavering gaze.

lines.japanese: 「なんでなんすか？」
lines.english: “So why are you like that with her?”

lines.japanese: 「つーかさ、なんであいつ言いかえさないんだよ。私はあいつが言いたいこと言えるように、わざわざヒールになってやってんのに」
lines.english: “More to the point, why won't she talk back? I'm going out of my way to play the villain so she'll finally say what she wants to say.”

lines.japanese: 以前、俺がマニュアルで苦しんでいたとき、英里子さんが助けようとしてくれたことを思いだしました。
lines.english: I remembered the time Eriko had tried to help me when I was struggling with the manual.

lines.japanese: 英里子さんの行動は、分かりにくいかもしれないけど、芯が通ってる。彼女の行動には誠意がある。根底に優しさがある。俺はそう思っています。
lines.english: Eriko's methods could be hard to understand, but there was a principle behind them. She acted in good faith. Underneath it all was kindness. That was what I believed.

lines.japanese: だけど、それが行きすぎて相手を傷つけてしまうこともしばしばあって、いまの日和子さんはそれに耐えられるほど強くない――少なくとも、彼女の不安を知っている俺にはそう感じられました。
lines.english: But often that kindness went too far and wounded the person she meant to help. Hiyoko was not strong enough to endure it now—or so it seemed to me, knowing the fear she carried.

lines.japanese: ま、好きな女の子を守りたいってのは、もちろんあるんですけどね。
lines.english: Of course, I also wanted to protect the girl I loved.

lines.japanese: 「人にはそれぞれタイプがあるじゃないすか。ぶつかるのが怖いひとだっているんすよ」
lines.english: “Different people handle things differently. Some are afraid of confrontation.”

lines.japanese: 「でもだよ？　言いたいこと言わずにずーっと溜めてるより、相手に向かって言った方が後腐れないでしょ」
lines.english: “But isn't it better to face someone and say what you want than to bottle it up forever? Then there's no bad blood afterward.”

lines.japanese: 「あいつだって、私がこんだけ言ってんだから何でも言えばいいんだよ。私は友達と壁を作りたくないの」
lines.english: “After all I've said to her, she should feel free to tell me anything. I don't want walls between me and my friends.”

lines.japanese: 「素晴らしい。英里子さんオトナっすねえ。ん、でもね、日和子さんの方は頭がいいだけで、精神的にはまだ発展途上なんすよ。少しは気ぃ抜いてあげてください」
lines.english: “Admirable. You're very mature, Eriko. But Hiyoko's smart; emotionally, she's still growing. Give her a little room to breathe.”

lines.japanese: 「理論武装されたオトナにそんな隙のない言い方で道塞がれたら、まっすぐな子供は逃げるほかありませんって」
lines.english: “When a grown woman armed with airtight logic blocks every road like that, a guileless kid has no choice but to run.”

lines.japanese: 「逃げんなよ、ドンと来いよ。でなきゃあいつ、自分で書いたものにだって自信持てないだろ」
lines.english: “Then don't run. Come at me head-on. Otherwise, how will she ever learn to believe in her own writing?”

lines.japanese: 「顔も見えないやつらの適当な言葉にいちいちビクついちゃってさ。もっと打たれづよくなんなきゃ、この先あいつやってけないって。進めば進むほど見えない敵は増えるんだし」
lines.english: “Every offhand remark from some faceless stranger makes her flinch. If she doesn't toughen up, she'll never survive. The farther she advances, the more invisible enemies she'll have.”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫ですってば。英里子さんは急ぎすぎなんです。あの子が本当の意味で強くなるまで、うちらは長い目で見守ってあげましょうよ」
lines.english: “She'll be all right. You're rushing her. Let's give her time and watch over her until she finds real strength of her own.”

lines.japanese: 英里子さんは座っていた椅子に背中を預け、フンと鼻を鳴らしました。
lines.english: Eriko leaned back against the sofa and snorted.

lines.japanese: 「友達の真面目ないちゃもんぐらいで逃げだしてんじゃねーっつの、チクショ」
lines.english: “Don't run away over one serious complaint from a friend, damn it.”

lines.japanese: それは目の前にいる俺ではなく、ここにいない誰かに放たれた言葉でした。
lines.english: Those words weren't meant for me, though I was right in front of her. They were aimed at someone who wasn't there.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、もし逃げないで立ちむかってきたら、友達の英里子さんはちゃんと受けとめてあげるんですか？」
lines.english: “Then if she stops running and faces you, will her friend Eriko accept whatever she has to say?”

lines.japanese: 「おー言えよ。なんでも受けとめてやるよ。ムカついたら倍にして言いかえすけど」
lines.english: “Damn right. She can say anything she likes, and I'll take it. Though if she pisses me off, I'll give her twice as much back.”

lines.japanese: 「ダメじゃん」
lines.english: “That defeats the purpose.”

lines.japanese: 「ダメじゃないでしょ、お互い言いたいこと言ってすっきりすればよくない？　あいつだって、私のことムカつくンならそう言やいいんだよ」
lines.english: “No, it doesn't. Why can't we both say what we think and get it out of our systems? If I piss her off, she should damn well tell me.”

lines.japanese: 「つーかさ、そもそも敬語ってのが気に入らない。年下ったって、ただのバイト同士なのに、なに壁作ってんだよ。そんなんじゃ言いたいことも言えないだろ」
lines.english: “And another thing—I hate how formal she is with me. She may be younger, but we're both just part-timers. Why put up a wall between us? Of course she can't say what she wants like that.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それは同意できないなー。敬語イコール壁なんて、それは英里子さんの認識がおかしッすよ」
lines.english: “Yeah, I can't agree with that. Using polite language doesn't mean you're putting up a wall. I think you've got that wrong, Eriko.”

lines.japanese: 「そーかあ？　私はなんか壁を感じるね」
lines.english: “You think? It feels like a wall to me.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ英里子さん、俺に対していつも壁を感じてたんすか」
lines.english: “Then have you always felt there was a wall between you and me?”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　いや、それはねーけど」
lines.english: “Hmm? No, I haven't.”

lines.japanese: 「ほら。じゃあ日和子さんが敬語だっていいじゃないすか」
lines.english: “There you are. Then there's nothing wrong with Hiyoko being formal with you.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、ほんとだ……」
lines.english: “Huh. You're right...”

lines.japanese: 「ね？　だからこんなん、英里子さん側の意識の問題でもあるんですよ。アナタも気付かないうちに壁作ってたんじゃないですか」
lines.english: “See? So part of this lies in your own attitude. Maybe you put up a wall without realizing it.”

lines.japanese: 「つか、ハッ……おまえさあ」
lines.english: “Wait—ha. You know...”

lines.japanese: 英里子さんが少し呆れたような表情を浮かべました。
lines.english: Eriko gave me a slightly exasperated look.

lines.japanese: 「いくら好きだからって、たまひよのこと可愛がりすぎじゃない？　そんなんじゃ、いつまで経ってもあいつ一人立ちできないよ」
lines.english: “Aren't you coddling Tama-chick too much just because you're in love with her? At this rate, she'll never learn to stand on her own.”

lines.japanese: 「てへ」
lines.english: “Oopsie.”

lines.japanese: 「きめぇ！　なんだその笑い、うーわ、やっぱこんなのたまひよとくっつけちゃいけない気がしてきた」
lines.english: “Disgusting! What was that? Ugh, now I'm thinking maybe I shouldn't let anything like you get together with Tama-chick after all.”

lines.japanese: 「おお、やっぱりアナタ日和子さんのこと心配してくれてるんすねえ。あー良かった」
lines.english: “Oh, so you really are worried about her. What a relief.”

lines.japanese: 「心配っつーか、だから私はたまひよのこと、べつに嫌いじゃないって前から言ってんじゃん」
lines.english: “Worried or whatever—I've told you before that I don't dislike Tama-chick.”

lines.japanese: 「あいつも入ってきた当初は可愛げあったんだよ。仕事覚えるまではしょっちゅう英里子さぁ～んとか言って泣きついてきたりさ」
lines.english: “She was even kind of cute when she first started. Until she learned the job, she was always running to me in tears, crying, ‘Erikooo!’”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ……ええっ、アナタそれ、可愛げなんてレベルじゃないすよ！」
lines.english: “Wait... What!? That goes far beyond ‘kind of cute’!”

lines.japanese: 「ン……まあなァ……」
lines.english: “Mm... Well, yeah...”

lines.japanese: 「それがちょっと厳しく指導してたら、いつの間にか反抗的ンなっちゃって──」
lines.english: “Then I got a little strict while training her, and before I knew it she'd turned rebellious—”

lines.japanese: 「──や、違うな、反抗的ならまだいいのに、何も言いかえしてこないんだよ。私はさ、ただ、あいつがそんなふうに、私に対して言いたいことも言ってくれないのが、なんつーか……」
lines.english: “—no, that isn't right. Rebellion would be fine. She doesn't talk back at all. I just... When she won't tell me anything she actually wants to say, it makes me feel... I don't know...”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、なんだ、要は寂しんすね」
lines.english: “Oh, I see. Basically, you're lonely.”

lines.japanese: 「ばっ……ばか、そんなんじゃねーっての！　な、なにが寂しいだ、へーん、寂しくなんかないですぅー！　なに言ってんのバーカ！　バーカバーカ！　ウルトラバーカ！」
lines.english: “I—idiot! That's not it at all! Wh-what do you mean, lonely? Hmph! I am not lonely! What are you talking about? Idiot! Idiot, idiot! Biggest idiot in the world!”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、このひとも子供だ！」
lines.english: “Whoa. This one's a child too!”

lines.japanese: 英里子さんは照れかくしのつもりか、幼稚な反撃をしてきました。ここいらで引いておいた方が良さそうです。
lines.english: Apparently hoping to hide her embarrassment, Eriko launched a juvenile counterattack. It seemed wise to retreat at this point.

lines.japanese: もう英里子さんの言いたいことも充分わかりましたしね。
lines.english: Besides, I understood everything she wanted to say now.

lines.japanese: まったく、なーにが「べつに嫌いじゃない」ですか。アナタ日和子さんのこと大好きなんじゃないですか。
lines.english: Honestly, what was this nonsense about ‘not disliking’ Hiyoko? She clearly adored her.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、俺はフロアに戻りますよ。いくら今は混んでないって言っても、三人も抜けちゃ人手が足りないですからね」
lines.english: “Well, I'm going back to the floor. Even if we aren't busy now, we'll be short-handed with three people gone.”

lines.japanese: 俺が立ち上がると、英里子さんもやや動きの重そうな仕草で腰を浮かせました。
lines.english: When I stood, Eriko too rose from the sofa, though her movements seemed a little heavy.

lines.japanese: 「フゥ……そーね、私も行くよ」
lines.english: “Sigh... Yeah. I'm coming.”

lines.japanese: 「でも千歳、私はたまひよが帰ってきたら同じこと言うよ。今だって結局また仕事ほっぽり出してんだから」
lines.english: “But Chitose, when Tama-chick comes back, I'm going to tell her exactly the same thing. Even now, she's abandoned her work again.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、分かってます。でも俺も、英里子さんが間違ってると思ったらすぐに割って入りますからね」
lines.english: “I know. But if I think you're wrong, I'll step between you immediately.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんとさっきキスしたこと、日和子さんが飛びだしちゃったこと、日和子さんの作品のことなんかが、ぐるぐる俺の頭を回っていました。
lines.english: The kiss Hiyoko and I had shared, her running off, her writing—all of it spun round and round inside my head.

lines.japanese: でも、結局のところは日和子さん次第なのかな。
lines.english: But in the end, perhaps everything depended on Hiyoko herself.
“Sigh…”

lines.japanese: 前髪を吹きあげながら今日も思う。
lines.english: I blew my bangs out of my eyes and found myself thinking, as I so often did:

lines.japanese: やっぱ人間関係って歯がゆいなあ。
lines.english: Human relationships really were frustrating things.
